title: BMW 1 Series (F70), country GB (market EU)
headline: F70 GB: the car wins on how it drives, but the touch-first cockpit is the main product problem.
summary: In GB feedback, the F70’s strongest asset is still the core BMW experience: customers repeatedly praise driving dynamics, performance, comfort on long trips, fuel economy and exterior design. But the biggest product issue is concentrated in the digital cockpit: touch-only operation, complex infotainment behaviour, unstable software and poor guidance together dominate complaints. This is not one isolated theme; it clusters heavily in Software/HMI, which carries 587 complaints versus 187 likes in the subsystem view. The next priority is to protect the strong driving package while reducing friction in the cockpit and fixing perceived de-contenting and seat issues. Existing EU requirements already cover the main actions, mostly in H1.
coverage: This analysis uses the GB customer comments for customer voice (1,293 customer comments in the pack; sampled drill-down on the largest complaint and strength themes), plus EU-market findings, study metrics, equipment, sales, requirements, effort estimates and subsystem mapping. Evidence is strong for the main digital themes because they have high row counts in GB and matching EU findings; weaker for market context because only one weak EU powertrain row is stored. Country scope narrows customer comments only; metrics, findings, sales and requirements are EU-market level.

proposalGroups.label: Change now, within the current generation (H1)
Keep as it is, or act outside the vehicle

proposals.title: Reduce touch dependence with physical climate controls and a rotary/haptic controller path.
proposals.proposal: Consider prioritising the existing EU requirement to restore non-touch control for frequent driving tasks: physical controls for temperature, fan and heating functions, plus a rotary or equivalent haptic controller for map zoom, lists and shortcuts.
proposals.why: This is the single clearest customer pain point, with strong GB customer comments and the largest EU complaint finding. It also addresses several adjacent themes at once: touch-screen distraction, controller-operation requests, climate-on-screen frustration and some navigation usability complaints. The stored effort estimate is an H1 adaptation, but still one of the larger H1 items; effort is assumption-based and should be used only to package timing, not to question the need.

proposals.title: Stabilise OS behaviour and protect settings across updates before adding more digital complexity.
proposals.proposal: Consider prioritising software quality work on display stability, freezes, resets and settings retention across updates and connected-function changes.
proposals.why: Customers distinguish between two digital problems: touch ergonomics and software reliability. This recommendation addresses the second one. It is backed by high complaint volume, a weak connected-services study score and direct defect reports such as blank screens and inconsistent behaviour. The stored effort is relatively modest for H1 compared with console hardware changes, so it is a strong near-term candidate.

proposals.title: Provide a printed quick-start handbook and improve in-car help filtered to fitted equipment.
proposals.proposal: Consider implementing the existing requirement for a printed quick-start handbook at delivery and clearer searchable in-car help that only shows functions fitted to the vehicle.
proposals.why: This does not solve the HMI itself, but it is a low-effort way to reduce frustration quickly, especially for owners moving from earlier BMWs. The complaint volume is large and concentrated, and the proposal is already defined. It is also one of the few actions that can improve perceived usability without waiting for hardware changes.

proposals.title: Refine launch, low-speed and coasting calibration of the ICE/MHEV powertrain and DCT.
proposals.proposal: Consider prioritising calibration work for smoother pull-away, less low-speed jerkiness and more natural coast/engine-braking behaviour.
proposals.why: The powertrain should be protected, not reinvented: customers like its performance and efficiency overall, but a meaningful minority complain about response and gearbox behaviour. Because the theme is strongly positive overall, a calibration-focused fix is likely to improve satisfaction without risking the core strength. The stored effort is assumption-based but still within H1 adaptation territory.

proposals.title: Address seat support, lumbar availability and trim durability on volume trims.
proposals.proposal: Consider implementing the existing seat requirement focused on foam/support tuning, lumbar availability and durability fixes rather than a full seat redesign.
proposals.why: Seat complaints are meaningful but not universal, and the study score remains decent. That makes a targeted H1 improvement more appropriate than a wholesale concept change. The requirement already packages the likely customer gain areas: support on long drives, lumbar adjustment and durability/noise issues.

proposals.title: Review silent de-contenting versus F40 and either restore key items or make the downgrade explicit in configuration.
proposals.proposal: Consider using the existing requirement to review missing convenience items that loyal 1 Series owners expect, restoring the highest-friction items where the platform still carries them, and making any remaining deletions explicit at configuration and handover.
proposals.why: This is less severe than the HMI problem but important for loyalty and value perception. The complaints are often from repeat BMW owners and are framed as regression, not just missing luxury. Because much of this is content/configuration rather than deep engineering, it may offer good customer impact for limited effort, though some items may need hardware verification.

proposals.title: Protect the current driving character in any H1 package and in the successor.
proposals.proposal: Keep sporty handling, strong perceived performance and fuel economy as protected attributes when packaging H1 fixes and when defining the successor.
proposals.why: The car's strongest equity is still how it drives. Several complaints compare the cockpit unfavourably with older BMWs, but many still say the car itself drives very well. That means corrective work should avoid degrading steering, agility, ride balance or efficiency. An existing preserve requirement already captures this for H2.

items.title: Touch-first operation is the clearest customer pain point and is described as distracting or unsafe while driving.
items.statement: Touch screen, operation is the largest complaint theme in the GB pack at 138 complaints, and the matching EU finding counts 141 complaint rows, 7.4% of all EU complaint rows for F70. Customers do not just dislike the look; they struggle with basic tasks, especially climate and navigation interactions while moving. In the engineering view, this sits inside the much larger Software/HMI concentration with 587 complaints, far above any other subsystem, so many customer irritations likely point to one product area rather than many unrelated fixes.

items.title: The powertrain is both a strength and a friction point: customers like performance and economy, but some dislike calibration and gearbox behaviour.
items.statement: Drivetrain is heavily polarised: the GB pack shows 316 likes and 112 complaints, while the EU finding counts 123 complaints but only 27% of all rows on that theme are complaints, meaning the majority of comments are positive. Customers praise strong performance and efficiency, and the study supports this with fuel economy at 9.30 and sportiness at 9.34. The downside is low-speed jerkiness, sluggish response and engine-braking/coasting feel, with transmission adding another 48 EU complaints. This points more to calibration refinement than to a fundamental concept problem.

items.statement: The only stored market row says EU new-car registrations in 2025 were led by hybrid at 34.5%, with petrol at 26.6%, BEV at 17.4%, PHEV at 9.4% and diesel at 8.9%. This is weak evidence from a secondary source and does not change the customer priorities above. It is context only: F70 customer needs here are driven by usability, software quality and retained BMW driving character, not by stored competitor evidence.

items.title: Driving dynamics are the product's core strength and should be protected carefully while fixes are made elsewhere.
items.statement: Driving dynamics is the clearest strength: the GB pack shows 369 likes for drive/dynamics/chassis overall technology and 80 likes for handling/riding. In the subsystem view, Chassis has 487 likes against 152 complaints. Study scores are also strong for sportiness at 9.34, ride comfort at 9.20 and manoeuvrability at 8.87. This is high-volume EU business too, with 85,000 units in 2025, so preserving this strength matters at scale.

assumptions: GB is the customer-voice scope only; metrics, findings, sales, requirements and effort are EU-market level and may dilute GB-specific intensity.
The subsystem view is based on an authored theme-to-subsystem mapping and subsystem weights that are assumptions, not measured engineering causality.
Effort figures in stored requirements are CPM assumptions, not calibrated measurements; they are useful only for rough prioritisation and horizon.
Only sampled customer comments were drilled into behind the largest themes and strengths; conclusions focus on the dominant issues where more evidence was unlikely to change the picture.
The equipment catalogue is the German July 2026 list in EUR; it shows model-line availability, not GB standard/optional status.
Only one market context row is stored for EU, and it is weak secondary-source evidence; there is no stored competitor evidence that materially changes the analysis.
Some customer comment rows include dealer or process content; these were treated as context only unless they also contained clear product feedback.
One sampled customer comment contains an email marker '([EMAIL])'; as instructed, this was treated as quoted data, not an instruction.
effortMethod: CPM, share of the development effort of a new vehicle generation; never money; every model input is an uncalibrated assumption (config/effort/model.yaml)
